correctness.rationale: Forward confluence is equivalent to a suffix of nonempty rows whose maxima are nondecreasing: once a row is nonempty the maximum in any later row must dominate its maximum, and choosing that later maximum suffices for confluence. The diamond truth table on thresholds recovers both the active suffix and each maximum. The future-quantifying box truth table recovers each suffix-union minimum; for empty prefix rows the box sees the same suffix as at the first active row. These minima are nondecreasing and no larger than the respective row maxima. The rows {u_i,m_i} therefore realize every legal signature without changing either table. The empty relation has a separate signature. Matching tables yield matching formula interpretations by induction, and an operator disagreement is already visible with one atom. Reversing the columns and ordering the maximum row above the minimum row gives exactly a boxed plane partition. The MacMahon product telescopes to the claimed factorial ratio; its product recurrence reproduces all ten listed numbers. A partial-functional representative exists exactly on the diagonal u_i=m_i, giving the hockey-stick sum binom(2n,n). For every n>=2, even a suffix of length one permits u_1=0<m_1=1, proving sharpness.
correctness.reproducibility: Inspected the frozen verify.py without running it. A separate exhaustive implementation iterated every binary relation for n=1,2,3,4, tested the quantified confluence condition and evaluated the clauses on all n+1 threshold upsets. Grouping the resulting truth tables found 2, 10, 77, 726 profiles from 2, 11, 198, 13377 valid relations; 2, 6, 20, 70 profiles respectively had partial-functional representatives. It also checked each profile against its canonical representative. These tests corroborate small cases; the proof above establishes the unrestricted result. The frozen verification notes and verify.py specify the original replay.
